title: Ten years, tens of millions of cells - Nature Biotechnology
gist: On the Human Cell Atlas's tenth anniversary, the piece traces its growth from ~100 researchers in 2016 to 4,000+ members in 100+ countries and sets out HCA 2.0: 3D multimodal maps, disease focus, greater diversity, and AI foundation models aiming at a 10-billion-cell atlas and virtual tissue models over the next decade.

insights.claim: The Human Cell Atlas began in October 2016 when around 100 researchers, led by Aviv Regev and Sarah Teichmann, set the goal of mapping every cell in the body's roughly 30 trillion cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Provides the baseline for judging a decade of scale-up in single-cell biology.
insights.quote: a group of around 100 researchers set the audacious goal of mapping every cell in the human body

insights.claim: Fixed pipelines and parameters could not analyse single-cell variation across tissues, so the HCA set broad standards that each organ, tissue or system must meet, with tailored collection strategies and integration methods.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Standards and comparable cell annotations are what make datasets integrable, a lesson for any data-consortium effort.
insights.quote: it was not possible to successfully analyze single-cell data variation with fixed pipelines and parameters

insights.claim: Droplet-based sequencing with cellular barcodes plus Smart-seq2 and CEL-seq2 meant that by late 2016 gene expression could be routinely quantified in tens of thousands of single cells at manageable cost.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cost and throughput of single-cell tools enabled the atlas and the instrument and reagent market behind it.
insights.quote: By late 2016, it was possible to routinely quantify gene expression in tens of thousands of single cells with high accuracy at manageable costs.

insights.claim: Dissociating tissue for sequencing loses cell location, which spatial transcriptomics (annealing fixed tissue to barcoded reverse transcriptase primers) overcame while keeping positional information.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Spatial biology fills the main gap in dissociated single-cell data and is a growth segment for tools vendors.
insights.quote: in dissociating a tissue into single cells for sequencing, information about the cell’s original location within the tissue was lost

insights.claim: Today spatial technologies can map thousands of RNAs simultaneously and can incorporate protein, metabolite and lipid locations within a cell or large tissue area.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Multiplexed multi-omic spatial readouts underpin the planned shift to 3D multimodal maps.
insights.quote: Today, spatial technologies can map thousands of RNAs simultaneously
insights.locator: The HCA defined how to test

insights.claim: By 2024 the HCA community had launched four integrated v1 atlases: the Human Lung Cell Atlas, whole-brain and cortical atlases from the NIH BRAIN Initiative, and the Human Retina Cell Atlas.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Shows the consortium has moved from pilots to integrated reference atlases usable by drug developers.

insights.claim: The integrated HLCA v.1 contains over 2 million cells from the respiratory tracts of 486 individuals, drawn from 49 datasets generated by the wider research community.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Community-submitted datasets scaling into one reference demonstrates the integration model.
insights.quote: The integrated HLCA v.1 contains over 2 million cells from the respiratory tracts of 486 individuals, from 49 different datasets

insights.claim: During COVID-19, HCA data from millions of cells let scientists identify tissues expressing genes relevant to SARS-CoV-2 viral entry and activation, though more work is needed to turn lung-disease data into therapeutic discovery.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Atlas data have shown real-world clinical utility, but target and biomarker discovery value remains to be proven.
insights.quote: but more work is needed to identify how these data can be used for therapeutic discovery

insights.claim: HCA 2.0 will extend the atlas to spatial and multimodal data, wider age, geographic and ethnic diversity, and a more systematic focus on specific diseases beyond today's healthy reference data.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A disease-focused phase makes the atlas more directly relevant to target discovery and biomarkers.
insights.quote: The next phase, HCA 2.0, will focus on extending the atlas in several directions
insights.locator: This is where the field is

insights.claim: The HCA has provided much of the cell and tissue data used to train the foundation models deployed by the research community today.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Open reference datasets are a key input to biology foundation models, giving data ownership and access strategic value.
insights.quote: the HCA has provided much of the cell and tissue data used to train the foundation models deployed by the research community today
insights.locator: AI models will be at the heart

insights.claim: Perturbational studies, human genetics and longitudinal data will let AI models predict at scale what happens when a cell changes, such as a gene deletion or drug exposure, turning the HCA from a static map into a predictive model of human biology.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Predictive virtual-cell models are the pitch for AI-driven drug discovery; track whether predictions are validated.
insights.quote: transforming the HCA from a static map into a predictive model of human biology

insights.claim: The HCA now has over 4,000 members from more than 100 countries, with regional groups in Asia, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East, and HCA 2.0 disease choices will align with the needs of low- and middle-income countries.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Diverse representation improves generalisability of atlas-trained models and therapeutics across populations.
insights.quote: The HCA now has over 4,000 members from more than 100 countries

insights.claim: The consortium targets an atlas of 10 billion cells and virtual tissue models over the next decade, versus the millions of cells catalogued today.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A thousand-fold scale-up implies sustained demand for sequencing, spatial and compute infrastructure.
insights.quote: Generating an atlas of 10 billion cells and creating virtual tissue models over the next decade is ambitious
